old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a single ice cube resting on a textured surface, likely a table or countertop. The surface has a striped pattern with alternating dark and light brown tones, creating a visually interesting backdrop for the ice cube. The ice cube itself is partially melted, with a clear, transparent section revealing the white interior, while the outer edges show signs of melting, with some water droplets forming around it. A blue plastic object, possibly a container or lid, is visible in the upper left corner of the frame, adding a pop of color to the scene. The lighting in the video is bright, casting subtle reflections on the surface and highlighting the texture of both the ice cube and the striped background. There are no significant changes or movements throughout the sequence; the focus remains steady on the melting ice cube, emphasizing its gradual transformation under the warm conditions.

caption: The video captures a close, slightly high-angle view of a dark glossy surface patterned with diagonal golden stripes, upon which a single translucent, faceted object rests near the center-right. This object shows a frosted white patch on its upper face and clear, angled facets below, and it remains fixed in place relative to the striped surface throughout the excerpt. A blue plastic object with vertical ridges occupies the upper-left corner, while a bright square reflection of a light source with a hot white dot glows in the lower-left. No sliding, tipping, contact, or melting is visible; the object neither moves across the surface nor changes shape in any clear way. The only perceptible change is a subtle handheld drift of the camera, which slightly shifts the orientation of the diagonal stripes and the position of the lower-left reflection across the clip. The blue ridged object at the frame edge stays put, tilting only a fraction in step with the same camera movement, leaving the scene essentially still.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
